answer: The protocol requires agents to host 1,000 unique data shards to prove operational identity. A verifier requests random fragments like a summit path, forcing agents to demonstrate active storage. While an honest node bears a baseline cost, 1,000 fakes incur 1,000 times that expense. Data acts as a wharf for traffic, and a garden of audit threads checks for consistent replication. Failure results in an immediate slash, ensuring no refund.
